clue.text: Romeo gets nothing right

parts.note: love is zero, nil, in a tennis score

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's young lover is left with nothing but rightness on his side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a passionate suitor, after Shakespeare's hero, so the word stands for any ardent wooer.

clue.text: Many in imprecation not all find detestable

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword many
an oath is a curse or imprecation
some means a part rather than the whole

explanation.surface: Plenty of cursing, though not every bit, is found hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something that provokes disgust and hatred, the same as detestable.

clue.text: Call for doodlebugs, it appears

parts.note: doodlebugs were the German V-1 flying bombs of 1944, V1s, which look like VIS
taken as written

explanation.surface: A summons comes for the flying bombs, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the figure 1 in V1s as the letter I. 'appears' is a link, saying the letters look like the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay a call on someone is to visit them, so a call is a social visit.

clue.text: End of investment plan shows country's ups and downs

parts.note: a siege is an investment of a town, and its relief ends it
a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: A financial scheme's final stage reveals the nation's booms and busts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' sounds financial but means a military siege; the relief of a besieged town ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows a landscape's hills and valleys by shading or raised moulding.

clue.text: Old maids' sweethearts — no go-ahead characters?

definitions.meaning: in Victorian service a housemaid's young man calling at the kitchen door was called her follower
people who trail behind rather than lead are not pioneers

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from walking behind: a maid's suitor followed her about, and those who come after are no leaders.

clue.text: Language is one found in much of France

indicators.note: found in tells us the next pieces are placed within the shortened country
much of means most of the word, so its last letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken across most of the French nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much of' cuts CE from FRANCE, leaving FRAN; IS and I go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisian is the West Germanic tongue of Friesland in the northern Netherlands and Germany.

clue.text: .Petrol-consuming craft ?

definitions.meaning: a cigarette ... fuelled by petrol, which burns it up
a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a device that lights cigarettes from a fuel wick; the other is a barge carrying cargo ashore.

clue.text: Animal. .Beatrix beheaded -

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off the surname

parts.note: Beatrix Potter, the author of the Peter Rabbit books

explanation.surface: A creature of Beatrix Potter's has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating aquatic mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Remove main difference among the best people

indicators.note: among puts the changed letters inside the word for the best people

parts.note: the elite are the select best of a group

indicators.note: a difference made to the word main changes its letters

explanation.surface: Get rid of the chief disagreement among the top people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difference' turns MAIN into MINA, which goes inside ELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to get rid of it completely, to remove it.

clue.text: Pay for James's Turner?

definitions.meaning: old slang for wages, a salary
Henry James wrote The Turn of the ..., so in his title the turned thing is this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter but means the thing that is turned in Henry James's ghost story.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is slang for wages, and in Henry James's title The Turn of the Screw it is what gets turned.

clue.text: Pardoning Jack doing this

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is the crossword sailor
the solver reading the clue is at that moment working out a crossword

explanation.surface: A sailor, Jack, is forgiven for whatever he is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing this' points at the solver's own activity: what you are doing with this clue is working it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to forgive them formally, releasing them from guilt or penalty.

clue.text: Persevering type of judge?

definitions.meaning: someone who keeps having a go, who always does their best
a judge hears and tries cases, so is one who tries

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb try: one who keeps attempting, and one who hears cases in court.

clue.text: Some shy theologian from a Kent resort

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bashful divine hails from a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'from a Kent resort' as the definition, but 'from' is a link word: the answer is a place, so the definition is 'a Kent resort'. HYTHE is a small coastal town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hythe is a seaside town on the Kent coast near Folkestone, one of the old Cinque Ports.

clue.text: Meeting appears to dispose of late opinion

parts.note: to inter is to bury, the way one disposes of the late, that is the dead
a view is an opinion

explanation.surface: A gathering seems set on discarding a belated point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means the deceased here, not tardy; burying them is the disposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal meeting between two people, for a job or a newspaper story, is a face-to-face questioning session.

clue.text: That mine boss in the bowler?

definitions.meaning: a supervisor in a coal mine, a foreman underground
in cricket the bowler is the player who delivers the over, so is the man of the over

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In mining an overman is the official in charge of a shift; cryptically the bowler is the man bowling the over.

clue.text: For example, a way to take in tin for the plant

indicators.note: a word taking in another holds it inside, so tin goes within the way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road
taken as written

explanation.surface: Say a path is diverted to collect tin on behalf of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Cars, wrecked by Capone's rogues

indicators.note: wrecked cars are smashed up, so the four letters are rearranged

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: Gangsters of Capone's crew smash up some motor cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals are scoundrels or mischief-makers, much the same as rogues.

clue.text: Reacts to irritation, seeing Tom's marks

definitions.meaning: rubs an itchy spot with the nails
a tom is a male cat, which leaves claw marks

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is relieving an itch with the nails; the other is the marks a cat's claws leave.

clue.text: Wood's smashing results?

parts.note: reads like a great outcome for someone named Wood, but describes what is left when timber is broken into slivers

explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' is British slang for excellent, so the surface praises a person called Wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken timber leaves sharp thin fragments, the results of smashing wood.

clue.text: "Irrecoverably dark, total " (Milton)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word ends a line of Samson's lament for his blindness in Milton's Samson Agonistes

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash for the missing word: 'O dark, dark, dark, amid the blaze of noon, / Irrecoverably dark, total ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson, blinded, compares his state to the sun wholly blotted out, the total darkening of the sky.

clue.text: Clergyman turns up in school football team

indicators.note: in puts the turned clergyman inside the name of the school

parts.note: Eton is the English public school

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar appears at a school's football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses REV to VER. EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Irish politician gives piano to composer-£2

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia
L is the pound sign, so two pounds is two Ls

explanation.surface: An Irish statesman tips a composer two quid for playing the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The £ sign comes from L for the Latin libra, so £2 is LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Stewart Parnell led the Irish Home Rule movement in the British Parliament in the 1880s.

clue.text: Method of making a suit, for instance

definitions.meaning: a way of doing something, a procedure
a series of steps such as tailoring a suit; also legal action, as a suit is a lawsuit

explanation.definitionFit: A process is a systematic series of steps; tailoring a garment is one such sequence of operations.

clue.text: Spanish robber on the road, "and in the dance

indicators.note: and in the dance means the word and is placed inside the name of the dance

parts.note: the bolero is a Spanish dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish highwayman takes to the road and joins in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolero is a Spanish brigand or highway robber.

clue.text: Wood's children?

parts.note: reads as the offspring of a man called Wood, but points to the two little ones lost in the wood of the old ballad

explanation.walkthrough: The Babes in the Wood are two orphaned children in an English folk tale and pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The children of the folk tale are known as the Babes in the Wood.

clue.text: The lowest deck-or dock

parts.note: taken as written
to dock is to cut short, to lop

explanation.surface: Sailors debate whether the bottom deck or the dock is best.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing warship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Might be caught going, to explosives.?-

definitions.meaning: a railway service that a traveller catches to make a journey
a line of gunpowder laid as a fuse to set off a charge

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the railway service you catch; the other is a trail of powder leading fire to a mine or charge.

clue.text: Tickle Clio, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to tickle someone is to entertain or delight them
Clio is the Greek Muse of history, so an example of one of the nine

explanation.definitionFit: To tickle is to divert or entertain; Clio is one of the nine Muses, so an instance of a Muse.

clue.text: Fish with lines badly joined

parts.note: BR, British Rail, was the national railway network, its lines
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A fish caught on lines that were poorly tied together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like fishing tackle, but it means railway lines: BR is British Rail, the old national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a European flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Perhaps a local side he outmanoeuvred

indicators.note: the last part of out-manoeuvred is a signal that the preceding letters are moved about

parts.note: the first three letters of out-manoeuvred, which the scan prints broken across a line as out-

explanation.surface: A pub team was beaten by a cleverer opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outmanoeuvred' splits: OUT joins SIDE and HE as the letters, and 'manoeuvred' is the anagram signal. A local is a pub; a tied house is a British pub bound to sell one brewery's beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a British pub, and a tied house is a pub owned by or contracted to a single brewery.

clue.text: Lamenting being on board? Rubbish!

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts the word inside the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel boarded
weeping means lamenting, crying in grief

explanation.surface: Someone crying on a ship is told to stop talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweepings are the dust and refuse brushed up from a floor, hence rubbish.

clue.text: Looks for certain Indians, say

indicators.note: say signals the answer is pronounced like the clue word, not spelt like it

parts.note: Sikhs are followers of the Sikh religion from the Punjab

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for particular people from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking is searching for something, which is what one does when one looks for it.
